findings.reason: replacing the count with set equality of (file,line) against the enumeration, which the fragment already states per row, makes the check fail for a missing site whatever else the fragment contains.
findings.text: §4's endpoint is a row *count* equal to the lock-taking call count (43 of the 74 `fcntl.flock(` lines at 4d5c4389), and a count equality is invariant under one omitted site paired with one duplicated row, so the census can pass while a flock call is unaccounted for — the very claim the section exists to establish; the negative control removes a row and therefore exercises only the undercount direction

findings.reason: one clause fixing the tree on shared storage converts the head arm from a report that a path is absent — the base arm alone reveals the mistake, after a wasted round — into the lock evidence the section measures.
findings.text: §2's two-node arm requires the second invocation to reach "the same temporary tree" but does not say the tree must be on storage both nodes can open, while a worker's own brief directs temporary trees to node-local `$TMPDIR`; on a node-local tree the second node's "could not take the lock" is an ENOENT on the lock path, indistinguishable in the log from exclusion

response_events.note: §4's endpoint is now set equality: one row per lock-taking call by file and line, no call missing and none listed twice; the negative controls cover an omitted row and a duplicated row
